name: Tata Power Company Ltd
title: Tata Power Company Ltd - 500400 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Tata Power Q1 FY27 PAT up 11% to INR 1,401 cr with renewables capacity ramp to 2.5 GW in FY27 and capex of INR 5,300 cr in Q1 against INR 25,000 cr plan; curtailment near 5% and TP Solar supply-side discipline is a watch item.

summary.headline: Tata Power Q1 FY27 PAT rose 11% to INR 1,401 crore and EBITDA 8% to INR 4,249 crore, the 27th straight quarter of growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 PAT of INR 1,401 crore (+11%) and EBITDA of INR 4,249 crore (+8%), with revenue also up. Q1 capex was INR 5,300 crore, a first, against a FY27 plan of INR 25,000 crore. Odisha DISCOM collections were delayed by government payment timing and a heatwave-related disconnection pause, which management says is timing-related. Renewable capacity additions were 226 MW in Q1, with about 500 MW near commissioning and a FY27 target of 2,500-2,700 MW, taking installed capacity past 9 GW.

financial_highlights.change: first time quarterly spend at this level

financial_highlights.metric: Rooftop revenue (Q1, per analyst calculation from slides)
financial_highlights.change: revenue roughly doubled YoY per management

segments.name: Renewables (generation)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 6.7 GW, with 2.5 GW to be added in FY27 and capacity expected to cross 9 GW by year-end. Q1 commissioning was 226 MW; 500 MW is described as ready within weeks, with Q2 commissioning of 800-900 MW targeted.

segments.name: Rooftop solar
segments.commentary: Management guides to 60-70% growth this year. Q1 revenue was about INR 1,350 crore on 371 MW installed, and Mundra-style battery storage is being added. Management says cumulative rooftop revenue could reach INR 30,000 crore by 2029.

segments.name: Transmission (Mumbai and TBCB)
segments.commentary: Mumbai transmission has about INR 10,000 crore of regulated investment over five years. Two TBCB projects are near commissioning (Jalpura-Khurja now, Bikaner-Neemrana by October); TBCB revenue so far is construction-revenue booking, not line-by-line EBITDA.

segments.name: Distribution (Odisha and Delhi)
segments.commentary: Odisha PAT grew about 6% and units sold rose 10.4%, but collections were delayed by government payments, the heatwave disconnection pause and billing lag. Management says the DISCOM should be judged on a 12-month basis.

segments.name: Manufacturing (TP Solar)
segments.commentary: Module output crossed 1,000 MW in Q1 for the first time, while cell output fell after a line change. Margins are around 25-26%, and management expects yield and efficiency to peak in Q2.

segments.name: Tata Projects / solar EPC
segments.commentary: Third-party solar EPC has been discontinued and no new orders are being booked; remaining legacy projects are in final stages, and losses were booked in Q1. Management expects one more quarter of impact.

segments.name: Mundra (coal and power)
segments.commentary: Mundra's PAT rose on a higher share of coal profits, while EBITDA fell. The plant runs under a supplementary PPA on cost-reflective terms with no equity return. The state cabinet approvals are expected in August-September.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex plan of INR 25,000 crore, about 50% for renewables; Q2 capex expected above INR 6,000 crore, possibly INR 6,500 crore.
FY27 renewable additions of 2.5-2.7 GW, taking installed capacity past 9 GW by year-end.
Q4 is expected to be 4.5x-5x Q1 in profit terms, per management's trend comment.
Pumped storage: Shirwata 1,800 MW construction to start later in FY27; first 330 MW unit commissioning from early CY2029. Khorlochhu 600 MW Bhutan hydro expected in CY2030.
Rooftop: management expects cumulative revenue above INR 30,000 crore by 2029 and share rising from 12-13% to about 25%.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex of INR 5,300 crore, the first time it has reached this level in a quarter.
Renewables: 226 MW commissioned in Q1, 500 MW near ready; Q2 commissioning target 800-900 MW.
Pumped storage: 1,800 MW Shirwata construction to begin later in FY27. Dorjilung 1,125 MW financial closure with PFC, IFC and other lenders expected in about two months.
Transmission: over 2,000 km of transmission in the pipeline; Mumbai transmission investment about INR 10,000 crore over five years.
Module capacity: 1,000 MW+ output in Q1; cell capacity still ramping after a line change.
demand_pricing: Power demand grew about 8.5% in Q1 (May about 11%, June 9.8%); July ran at 260-270 GW.
Rooftop realisation: analyst calculated about INR 36/Wp billed versus about INR 28/Wp in order inflow; management attributed the gap to product mix (ULA scheme, module size), not a price decline.
Coal prices up about 5-7%, with management expecting up to 5% more over the next nine months.
Renewable auctions are muted as central agency (SECI, NHPC, NTPC) PPAs give way to direct state bids and FDRE/RTC tenders.
ALMM-II continues; management says the proviso for behind-the-meter projects covers about 10% of demand and does not affect its business.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Odisha DISCOM growth muted, and why did Tata Projects losses widen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited delayed government payments for drinking water and street lighting, a heatwave-driven pause in disconnections until 15 June, and billing lag. It expects a recovery in Q2. Tata Projects is closing legacy loss-making projects, with about 10% in the final stage and one more quarter of impact expected.

qa_highlights.question: Can curtailment losses be quantified, and when will transmission bottlenecks ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment across the industry was about 5% in Q1, which management says should settle over the next few quarters as evacuation lines are completed. Q2 commissioning should ramp up with about 500 MW near ready.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for renewable auction volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Central-agency auctions have slowed as states move to direct bids and customised FDRE/RTC tenders. Pumped storage and large C&I deals are the growth areas.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the TBCB EBITDA margin so low?
qa_highlights.answer: TBCB projects are still under construction, so revenue is recognised under lease accounting. Line-by-line EBITDA starts from Q2 as the two projects commission, with Q3 and Q4 to follow.

qa_highlights.question: Why did TP Solar margins rise, and will third-party cell sales continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party cell sales were small. Some sales may continue for a few quarters for ALMM-exempt or open-access projects, but management does not expect large sales ahead. Margins reflect higher-efficiency products.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Mundra PAT rise while EBITDA fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the PAT increase came from a higher share of coal profits. Under the supplementary PPA, the plant recovers coal costs and fixed costs on a normative basis but earns no equity return, so under-recovery is possible in some quarters.

risks_watch: Odisha and Delhi DISCOM collections are lagging and depend on timing; watch whether Q2 catches up.
Renewable commissioning is 500 MW away from the 2.5-2.7 GW FY27 target, and evacuation bottlenecks cause around 5% curtailment.
Rooftop growth (60-70% target) and falling module realisations as capacity rises across the industry; watch margins at TP Solar.
Net debt to underlying EBITDA is 3.41x against a 3x-plus capex plan; watch leverage against the guardrails.
Tata Projects losses are expected for one more quarter; the Mundra supplementary PPA leaves the plant without an equity return; the nuclear plan awaits government rules.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth, pipeline and rooftop, with repeated claims of consistency. It was defensive on Odisha collections, Tata Projects losses and the TBCB margin, attributing them to timing. It was brief on Mundra and EPC economics, and it deferred some detailed questions to Investor Relations.
key_quotes: This is the 27th consecutive quarter where we have seen increase in our PAT and EBITDA.
We will set up 2,500 megawatt to 2,700 megawatt.
We are at something like just 10% of the legacy projects in last stage there and cost to correction takes place because of that reason.
So in distribution, we should always look at 12 months rollover rather than seeing on a quarter-to-quarter basis.

adds.what: Renewable generation capacity additions, FY27 target 2.5-2.7 GW (6.7 GW installed today, to cross 9 GW by FY-end)
Renewable capacity: 226 MW commissioned in Q1; ~500 MW ready within weeks; Q2 target 800-900 MW
1,800 MW Shirwata pumped storage; first 330 MW unit from early CY2029
1,125 MW Dorjilung pumped storage, financial closure expected in about two months
Rooftop solar: 371 MW installed base, growing 60-70% in FY27 with battery storage being added

growth.why: FY27 renewable additions of 2.5-2.7 GW (from 6.7 GW to over 9 GW) and rooftop growth of 60-70% are guided, backed by 226 MW commissioned in Q1, ~500 MW near ready and a Q2 target of 800-900 MW, plus a INR 25,000 crore capex plan; Q1 EBITDA rose 8% and PAT 11%, but no revenue growth figure was given and DISCOM collections and solar EPC losses are headwinds.
